name: Edo
summary_text: In May 2018 in Ekpoma, Edo State, two men were discovered by their community; one was lynched to death and the other escaped. Coverage framed the killing around the local concept of an 'abominable act' defying 'the traditional laws and heritage of the land' — customary authority operating as a moral-jurisdiction mechanism outside the Sharia belt. No prosecution or accountability is recorded for the killing. The dossier groups Edo with Imo as the 'non-Sharia southeast/west belt' where violent community justice substitutes for formal enforcement. Score 0.024 below the national 0.08. The lynching is the most lethal single incident outside the Sharia block and the FCT, met with full impunity, qualifying under the 'state-implicated by omission' exception. On par with Imo (0.06), which pairs mob violence with a 2025 state-police operation; Edo's violence is more severe (death) but lacks a comparable recent state-enforcement event. Above the generic Sharia states (0.06, tied) by legal severity: Edo has no capital-punishment statute, but has demonstrated that extralegal lethal violence occurs with zero consequence.

sources.title: Abominable Act In Ekpoma Community: 2 Male Gay Lovers Caught Making Love, One Lynched To Death, Other Escaped – The Nigerian Observer
sources.claim_summary: Nigerian Observer news report (May 2018): in Ekpoma, Edo State, two men in their late twenties were discovered having sex by their community; one was lynched to death and the other escaped, in coverage framed around the local concept of an 'abominable act' defying 'the traditional laws and heritage of the land'. (Cache captured mostly page navigation; incident detail per the research dossier.) No prosecution is recorded for the killing.

The Initiative for Equal Rights (TIERs) '2024 Human Rights Violations Report' (published January 2025): annual documentation of violations based on real or perceived SOGIESC in Nigeria; per the dossier, its 2024 edition records 556 violations affecting 850 victims across the reporting period and states these represent only a fraction of the true scale.
